Requirement: The system shall report a soil moisture index (0–100 %, calibrated dry-to-saturated) at least once per minute, with repeatability of ±3 % index (1σ) at a fixed soil state.†
The system shall report ambient temperature (±1 °C) and relative humidity (±3 % RH) at least once per 5 minutes.
The system shall detect reservoir-low state when water falls below the level that leaves ≥ 150 mL above the pump intake.†

The system shall begin a watering episode when moisture falls below the dry threshold (default 35 %), continue cycles (subject to DI-06 and DI-07) until moisture exceeds the wet threshold (default 42 %), and shall not begin a new episode while moisture is between the thresholds. Thresholds are configurable per planter.
Each watering cycle shall deliver the configured dose (default 50 mL) within ±15 %.†
The system shall perform no more than the configured maximum automatic cycles per planter per rolling 24 h (default 2).
The system shall enforce a minimum interval between automatic cycles on the same planter (default 6 h).
The edge node firmware shall stop the pump no later than 30 s after any start command, independent of the supervisor.
The pump shall not run, and any running pump shall stop within 1 s, while reservoir-low is detected.
On sensor read failure or implausible moisture data (outside 0–100 % after calibration, or change > 20 %/min without a watering event), automatic watering shall be inhibited and a fault raised.
On loss of communication with the supervisor, the edge node shall turn the pump off and start no new cycles until the link is restored.
A single-point failure in the pump switching circuit (e.g. MOSFET shorted) shall not cause pumping to continue beyond 60 s.
If three consecutive watering cycles produce < 3 % moisture rise, the system shall inhibit automatic watering and raise a "no response" fault.

The dashboard shall show current moisture, temperature, humidity, reservoir state, pump state, last watering time and a 7-day moisture trend, shall flag any value older than 10 min as stale, and shall load in < 3 s over Tailscale.
The system shall show a reservoir-low alert on the dashboard within 60 s of detection and send a push notification.
The system shall log every sensor reading (≥ 1 per 5 min) and every pump event with a reason code, and retain logs ≥ 90 days.
A manual water command from the dashboard shall start the pump within 5 s, subject to DI-08 and DI-09.
The dashboard shall show a camera image of the planter (≥ 640 × 480) no older than 15 min.
All circuits shall operate at ≤ 12 V DC, powered by an external listed AC adapter, with a fuse on the 12 V line.
The electronics enclosure shall sit above the reservoir's maximum water line, and no water shall reach the electronics in a 250 mL splash test onto the enclosure top.†
The fluid path shall show no leaks over a 14-day run.
The reservoir shall hold enough water for ≥ 14 days at nominal use (≥ 1.5 L usable at 100 mL/day).†
The system shall run 14 days continuously without manual intervention or reboot.
The reservoir shall be refillable without tools in < 2 min through an opening ≥ 50 mm.
Adding planter N shall require only flashing the node firmware with its node ID and adding one config entry; no supervisor code change.
The dashboard shall be reachable only from the LAN and the tailnet, with no inbound router ports opened, and shall require login.
Footprint ≤ 300 × 200 mm; height ≤ 350 mm excluding the plant; the loaded unit shall not tip when tilted 10°.
A drip tray under the planter and reservoir shall contain ≥ 500 mL.†
Pump switching components shall operate at ≤ 50 % of rated current and stay below 60 °C case temperature during a 30 s run.

The system shall archive a planter image (≥ 640 × 480) at least once per hour and within 5 min after each watering cycle, store it only on the supervisor (no cloud upload), retain images ≥ 90 days, and let the user browse them by date on the dashboard.†
